LFHS Academic Hub — Class 9 Physics Second Term Examination (Answer Key & Solutions) Question 8 (3 Marks) Q: Give scientific reasons: (a) Passengers in a moving vehicle are advised to wear seat belts. (b) A cricketer moves his hands backward while catching a fast cricket ball. Answer & Explanation: (a) Why passengers wear seat belts: Based on Inertia of Motion (Newton's First Law). When a vehicle moves at high speed, the passengers share that forward velocity. In the event of sudden braking or collision, the passenger's lower body is brought to rest with the vehicle, but their upper body tends to keep moving forward due to inertia. Seat belts apply a safe restraining force, preventing passengers from striking the dashboard or windshield. (b) Why a cricketer pulls hands backward while catching: Based on Newton's Second Law of Motion (F = ∆p / ∆t).

By pulling hands backward, the cricketer increases the time interval (∆t) taken to bring the momentum of the ball to zero. Since force is inversely proportional to time, a longer time significantly reduces the rate of change of momentum, reducing the impact force on the hands and preventing injury. Question 12 (3 Marks) Q: Refractive indices: Water = 1.33, Kerosene = 1.44, Turpentine = 1.47, Crown Glass = 1.52.

(a) In which medium does light travel with maximum speed? Why? (b) A ray of light passes from turpentine into glycerol (refractive index 1.47) at an angle of incidence of 30°. What will be the angle of refraction? Explain. Answer & Explanation: (a) Medium with maximum speed of light: Water. Speed of light in a medium is given by v = c / n, where c is the speed of light in vacuum and n is the refractive index. Since refractive index is inversely proportional to speed, the medium with the lowest refractive index has the highest optical speed. Among the given media, Water has the lowest refractive index (n = 1.33). (b) Angle of refraction from turpentine into glycerol: Angle of refraction r = 30°. Reason: Refractive index of turpentine = 1.47 and refractive index of glycerol = 1.47. Since both media have identical refractive indices, their optical densities are exactly equal.

Therefore, light does not undergo any change in speed or deviation at the boundary. The ray passes undeviated through the interface, keeping r = i = 30°. Question 13 (3 Marks) Q: Identify which law of motion explains each of the following observations: (a) Recoil of a gun when a bullet is fired. (b) Dust particles fall off when a carpet is beaten with a stick. (c) High-jump athletes land on thick foam cushions or sand pits. Answer & Explanation: (a) Recoil of a gun when a bullet is fired: Newton's Third Law of Motion (To every action there is an equal and opposite reaction) & Law of Conservation of Linear Momentum. The forward force on the bullet produces an equal backward recoil force on the gun. (b) Dust falls off when a carpet is beaten with a stick: Newton's First Law of Motion (Inertia of Rest). When struck, the carpet moves forward suddenly, but the dust particles tend to remain in their state of rest due to inertia and separate.

(c) High-jump athletes landing on foam cushions or sand: Newton's Second Law of Motion (Impulse-Momentum Principle). The soft surface increases the deceleration time interval (∆t), which minimizes the rate of change of momentum and drastically reduces the impact force (F = ∆p / ∆t). Optical density The ability of a medium to influence the speed of light through it is its optical density. The speed of light decreases as optical density increases. The increasing order of optical densities of the media is given below. Air<Water<Glass<Diamond It is noted that a substance with high material density may not have high optical density. For example, the density of water is more than that of kerosene. However, the optical density of water is less than that of kerosene. Refraction Typically, light travels in a straight line. However, under certain conditions, it deviates from this path. See the figure.1 A light ray enters from air to water obliquely. The ray undergoes deviation at the surface of separation. It is noted that it doesn’t undergo deviation if the ray enters normally from one medium to another.

(See fig.2) When a ray of light enters obliquely from one medium to another with different optical densities, it undergoes deviation at the surface of separation. This phenomenon is called refraction. Cause of refraction Refraction of light is caused by the change in its speed when it passes from one medium to another. This change in speed occurs due to the change in the optical density of the medium. Refractive index:Refractive index of a medium is the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to the speed of light in the medium. Refractive index, n = c/v, where c – speed of light in vacuum & v – speed of light in the medium.

It is a vector quantity, meaning it has both magnitude (speed) and direction. The unit of velocity is m/s. • Uniform and Non-uniform Velocity: An object has uniform velocity if its magnitude of displacement is equal at equal intervals of time while moving in the same direction. Conversely, non-uniform velocity occurs if either the speed or the direction (or both) of an object's motion changes.

• Acceleration and Retardation: Acceleration is the change in velocity of an object in unit time, or the rate of change of velocity. It is also a vector quantity. When velocity decreases, it is termed negative acceleration or retardation. Its unit is also m/s². • Application in Road Safety and Accident Prevention: • Controlling Velocity and Acceleration. • Strictly following traffic rules is essential to reduce accidents. • Pedestrians also play a crucial role in road safety by following motion- based rules. They should walk along the right side of the road and cross only at designated zebra crossings, obeying traffic signals. Wearing light-coloured clothes in dim light is advisable as it increases visibility for drivers, reducing the risk of accidents caused by reduced perception of pedestrians. They provide crucial information about expected motion, speed changes, and potential hazards: • Mandatory Signs enforce compulsory rules, such as "No Parking" or "No Bicycles", guiding permissible movements. • Cautionary Signs warn drivers about upcoming road conditions like "Hump" or "Narrow Bridge," prompting them to adjust their velocity or acceleration. • Informatory Signs provide details like directions or distances to facilities, which aid in planning routes and maintaining a steady flow of traffic. • Road Markings, such as "Zebra crossings," define safe areas for specific movements, like pedestrian crossings or where vehicles can cross. ---------------------------------------------- 1.Graph related to the motion of a car is given below.
